list.name: contributor
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '(unattributed)') AS __text, COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '') AS __value FROM whodunit_repos ORDER BY 1
list.label: Contributor

options.content:
## Whodunit — AI Impact on Delivery
*Does AI assistance move delivery outcomes?* Adoption is measured from git history and the agent's own session records; delivery outcomes come from DevLake's DORA pipeline. Nothing here is self-reported.

**Read the scope before the numbers.** Adoption covers every instrumented repository. Delivery outcomes currently come from **EngageHub only** — it is the one project with deployments. Correlation panels state their sample size and withhold a coefficient until there are enough overlapping weeks to support one.

panels.title: Current adoption

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(c.status='assisted')*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0),1) v
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor'='__all__' OR r.contributor='$contributor')
  AND c.committed_at >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 7*86400) * 1000000000

panels.description: Share of the last 7 days' commits carrying an AI-Attribution trailer.

panels.title: Adoption over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       ROUND(SUM(c.status='assisted')*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0),1) AS `assisted %`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor'='__all__' OR r.contributor='$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description: The adoption curve. A flat line at zero before instrumentation is expected, not a gap in the data.

panels.title: Evidence strength

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE c.method
         WHEN 'intersected' THEN 'intersected — agent lines survived into the commit'
         WHEN 'observed'    THEN 'observed — agent touched the file, text changed since'
         WHEN 'declared'    THEN 'declared — stated, not measured'
         WHEN 'inferred'    THEN 'inferred — from surrounding evidence'
         ELSE 'undetermined — no evidence either way'
       END AS `method`,
       COUNT(*) AS `commits`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor'='__all__' OR r.contributor='$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY c.method ORDER BY commits DESC

panels.description: How strong the evidence is, not just how much there is. 'undetermined' means whodunit could not tell — it never means 'no AI was used'.

panels.title: Productivity — what can and cannot be concluded
Change size, assisted vs not
panels.description:
**This is a size difference, not a productivity gain.**

Mean lines changed per assisted commit against unassisted ones, within purposes where both sides have at least 20 commits — so `feature` is not being compared against `docs`.

A positive number means assisted commits are larger. Larger is not faster and not better: it may mean the agent takes on bigger work, or that it writes more code for the same outcome. Both are consistent with this figure.

Empty when no purpose has 20 commits on both sides, rather than showing a ratio computed from a handful.

**Deliberately not colour-coded.** Green for positive would assert that larger commits are better, which is the claim the panel beside this one exists to refuse.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(
  100.0 * (
    AVG(CASE WHEN c.status='assisted' THEN c.lines_added + c.lines_removed END)
    - AVG(CASE WHEN c.status='undetermined' THEN c.lines_added + c.lines_removed END)
  ) / NULLIF(AVG(CASE WHEN c.status='undetermined'
                      THEN c.lines_added + c.lines_removed END), 0)
, 0) AS v
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND c.purpose IN (
  SELECT purpose FROM (
    SELECT c2.purpose
    FROM whodunit_commits c2 JOIN whodunit_repos r2 ON r2.repo_id = c2.repo_id
    WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r2.contributor = '$contributor')
    GROUP BY c2.purpose
    HAVING SUM(c2.status='assisted') >= 20
       AND SUM(c2.status='undetermined') >= 20
  ) eligible
)

defaults.noValue: no purpose has 20+ commits on both sides

panels.title: Matched commits
panels.description:
The denominator behind the figure beside this — assisted against unassisted commits in the matched purposes.

Shown because a percentage without its sample size is not a measurement. Both sides must reach 20 before a purpose is included.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CONCAT(
  SUM(c.status='assisted'), ' vs ', SUM(c.status='undetermined')) AS v
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND c.purpose IN (
  SELECT purpose FROM (
    SELECT c2.purpose FROM whodunit_commits c2 JOIN whodunit_repos r2 ON r2.repo_id = c2.repo_id
    WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r2.contributor = '$contributor')
    GROUP BY c2.purpose
    HAVING SUM(c2.status='assisted') >= 20 AND SUM(c2.status='undetermined') >= 20
  ) eligible)

panels.title: Why this is not a productivity percentage

options.content:
### The comparison this dashboard cannot make

A productivity gain needs a **before** and an **after** of the same work. What exists here is assisted against unassisted commits *in the same period*, and the two are not the same population:

- **Selection is not random.** An agent is reached for on some kinds of work and not others. Measured on this data, 48% of assisted commits are features against 38% of unassisted ones — so an unmatched comparison partly measures which work got assigned to the agent.
- **Larger is not faster.** The only outcome here is change size. A bigger commit may be more work done or more code written for the same outcome.
- **No pre-adoption baseline is synced.** `dun baseline capture` records one locally — commits, cadence, median diff size, revert rate over a fixed window — but nothing publishes it, so the before-and-after comparison has no *before* to read. That is the comparison worth having: same repository, before and after, with the selection problem above absent by construction. Tracked as NAV-107.

The panels to the left control for purpose and show both sample sizes. That is as far as this data honestly goes.

panels.title: By agent

targets.rawSql:
SELECT c.agent AS `agent`, COUNT(*) AS `commits`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE c.status='assisted' AND c.agent<>''
  AND ('$contributor'='__all__' OR r.contributor='$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY c.agent ORDER BY commits DESC

panels.description: Which agent wrote the code. One slice means only one agent has produced commits here.

panels.title: Change size — assisted vs undetermined

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN c.status='assisted' THEN c.lines_added+c.lines_removed END),0) AS `assisted`,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN c.status<>'assisted' THEN c.lines_added+c.lines_removed END),0) AS `undetermined`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor'='__all__' OR r.contributor='$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description: Average lines changed per commit. Bigger assisted commits are a fact to explain, not automatically a win.

panels.title: Output tokens per 1,000 attributed lines
panels.description:
What the agent spent, in tokens, per thousand lines it wrote.

**This replaced a dollar figure** derived from a hand-typed monthly spend divided evenly over every line — an allocation dressed as a measurement, which reported the same unit cost whether the agent ran once or a thousand times, and defaulted to a $200 placeholder that was nobody's actual bill.

Tokens rather than currency, deliberately: under a subscription the marginal cost of a token is zero, so multiplying by an API rate would report money nobody spent — and nothing in a transcript says which billing model a user is on. Multiply by your own contract if you need a figure.

Empty where no session reported tokens: Antigravity reports none at all, and that is a property of the agent rather than a gap.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(
  (SELECT SUM(s.output_tokens)
     FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r2 ON r2.repo_id = s.repo_id
    WHERE s.output_tokens IS NOT NULL
      AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r2.contributor = '$contributor')
      AND s.last_seen >= $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000
      AND s.last_seen <  $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000)
  * 1000.0
  / NULLIF(SUM(e.lines_added + e.lines_removed), 0)
) AS v
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')
  AND e.observed_at >= $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000
  AND e.observed_at <  $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

defaults.noValue: no session reported tokens in this range

panels.title: Rework and cost per delivered unit
Fix-commit share by change size
panels.description:
**A rework proxy, not a defect rate.** `purpose` is derived from Conventional Commits prefixes and path heuristics, so this measures what commits were *labelled* — not what actually broke.

**Banded by change size, and that changes the answer.** The unbanded figure is 28.4% assisted against 33.3% unassisted, which looks favourable. Split by size it reverses in the middle band: assisted work is 42.1% fixes against 24.7% at 50-300 lines, while at under 50 lines it is 38.5% against 46.6%. The aggregate was a size-mix artefact — assisted commits skew larger, and large commits are rarely labelled fixes.

Both denominators are shown because several bands are thin. Selection bias is uncontrolled either way: an agent is reached for on some kinds of work and not others, so part of this measures which work was assigned rather than what the agent did to it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN c.lines_added+c.lines_removed < 50 THEN 'small (<50)'
     WHEN c.lines_added+c.lines_removed < 300 THEN 'medium (50-300)'
     ELSE 'large (300+)' END                                                          AS `Change size`,
  SUM(c.status='assisted')                                        AS `Assisted n`,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(c.status='assisted' AND c.purpose='fix')
    / NULLIF(SUM(c.status='assisted'),0),1)                       AS `Assisted fix %`,
  SUM(c.status='undetermined')                                    AS `Unassisted n`,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(c.status='undetermined' AND c.purpose='fix')
    / NULLIF(SUM(c.status='undetermined'),0),1)                   AS `Unassisted fix %`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE c.status IN ('assisted','undetermined') AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Output tokens per delivered line
panels.description:
Output tokens spent per line of assisted work that **reached a commit**.

The denominator is what distinguishes this from the token-per-attributed-line panel above: that one divides by agent activity, this one by work that shipped. Tokens spent on edits that were abandoned or rewritten count in the numerator and not the denominator, which is the point — that gap is the cost of work that did not land.

Tokens, never currency: under a subscription the marginal cost of a token is zero, so a price table would report money nobody spent.

Sessions and commits are counted over the same window but are not joined row-to-row — a session can span commits and a commit can span sessions. Read it as a rate for the period, not as an attribution per commit.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(
  (SELECT SUM(s.output_tokens)
     FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r2 ON r2.repo_id = s.repo_id
    WHERE s.output_tokens IS NOT NULL AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r2.contributor = '$contributor'))
  / NULLIF((SELECT SUM(c.lines_added + c.lines_removed)
     FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r3 ON r3.repo_id = c.repo_id
    WHERE c.status = 'assisted' AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r3.contributor = '$contributor')), 0)
) AS v

defaults.noValue: no tokens or no assisted lines in range

panels.title: Autonomy and what it produced
panels.description:
How much work happened at each level of autonomy.

**The session counts are thin and shown for that reason** — measured here, `default` is 3 sessions and `auto` is 1, against 64 for `never`. A mode with one session tells you about that session.

Tool calls are not shipped work. A mode that permits more actions produces more actions by construction; whether that becomes delivered code is the question this panel raises and cannot answer.

Each agent's own vocabulary is kept rather than mapped onto a shared enum — Codex says `never` and `on-request`, Claude Code says `acceptEdits`, `auto` and `default`.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  s.permission_mode          AS Mode,
  COUNT(*)                   AS Sessions,
  SUM(s.tool_calls)          AS `Tool calls`
FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = s.repo_id
WHERE s.permission_mode IS NOT NULL AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')
GROUP BY s.permission_mode ORDER BY SUM(s.tool_calls) DESC

defaults.noValue: no session recorded a permission mode

panels.title: Successful deployments

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cdc.cicd_deployment_id) v
FROM cicd_deployment_commits cdc
JOIN project_mapping pm ON cdc.cicd_scope_id = pm.row_id AND pm.`table` = 'cicd_scopes'
WHERE cdc.result='SUCCESS' AND cdc.environment='PRODUCTION'
  AND $__timeFilter(cdc.finished_date)

panels.description: Production deployments that succeeded, in the selected window.

panels.title: Change failure rate

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(cdc.result='FAILURE')*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0),1) v
FROM cicd_deployment_commits cdc
JOIN project_mapping pm ON cdc.cicd_scope_id = pm.row_id AND pm.`table` = 'cicd_scopes'
WHERE cdc.environment='PRODUCTION' AND $__timeFilter(cdc.finished_date)

panels.description: Failed production deployments as a share of all of them.

panels.title: Deployments in the denominator

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) v
FROM cicd_deployment_commits cdc
JOIN project_mapping pm ON cdc.cicd_scope_id = pm.row_id AND pm.`table` = 'cicd_scopes'
WHERE cdc.environment='PRODUCTION' AND $__timeFilter(cdc.finished_date)

panels.description: Shown next to the failure rate on purpose: a percentage without its denominator is how a handful of events becomes a headline.

panels.title: Median PR cycle time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(pr_cycle_time)/60.0, 1) v
FROM project_pr_metrics
WHERE pr_cycle_time IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(pr_merged_date)

panels.description: Open to merge. Check the PR count beside it before reading much into this.

panels.title: PRs measured

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM project_pr_metrics
WHERE pr_cycle_time IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(pr_merged_date)

panels.description: The sample size behind the cycle time to its left.

panels.title: Mean time to recovery

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, created_date, resolution_date))/60.0, 1) v
FROM incidents WHERE resolution_date IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(resolution_date)

panels.description: Blank means no issue is classified as an incident. That is an issue-tracker configuration gap, not a claim that nothing has broken.

panels.title: Deployment frequency

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(cdc.finished_date) AS `time`,
       COUNT(DISTINCT cdc.cicd_deployment_id) AS `deployments`
FROM cicd_deployment_commits cdc
JOIN project_mapping pm ON cdc.cicd_scope_id = pm.row_id AND pm.`table` = 'cicd_scopes'
WHERE cdc.result='SUCCESS' AND cdc.environment='PRODUCTION'
  AND $__timeFilter(cdc.finished_date)
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description: Successful production deployments per bucket.

panels.title: Deployment outcomes

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(cdc.finished_date) AS `time`,
       SUM(cdc.result='SUCCESS') AS `succeeded`,
       SUM(cdc.result='FAILURE') AS `failed`
FROM cicd_deployment_commits cdc
JOIN project_mapping pm ON cdc.cicd_scope_id = pm.row_id AND pm.`table` = 'cicd_scopes'
WHERE cdc.environment='PRODUCTION' AND $__timeFilter(cdc.finished_date)
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description: The failure rate's two components, so a rising rate can be read as more failures or fewer deployments.

options.content:
**How to read this section.** Each chart plots AI adoption against a delivery outcome over the same weeks. The `r` beside it is a correlation coefficient: `+1` means they rise together, `-1` means one rises as the other falls, `0` means no linear relationship.

**`r` is withheld until there are 10 overlapping weeks.** Below that it is arithmetic, not evidence — three points can produce `r = 0.99` from coincidence. The paired series still plots, so you can watch the relationship form. **Correlation is not causation** even at high `n`: a release freeze, a hiring round or a quarter boundary moves these numbers too.

panels.title: Adoption vs deployment frequency

targets.rawSql:
WITH a AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1000000000), '%x-W%v') AS wk,
       SUM(status='assisted')*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS adoption
FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY wk),
     m AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(cdc.finished_date, '%x-W%v') AS wk,
       COUNT(DISTINCT cdc.cicd_deployment_id) AS metric
FROM cicd_deployment_commits cdc
JOIN project_mapping pm ON cdc.cicd_scope_id = pm.row_id AND pm.`table` = 'cicd_scopes'
WHERE cdc.result='SUCCESS' AND cdc.environment='PRODUCTION' GROUP BY wk)
SELECT a.wk AS `week`, ROUND(a.adoption,1) AS `adoption %`, ROUND(m.metric,1) AS `deployments/wk`
FROM a JOIN m ON a.wk = m.wk ORDER BY a.wk

panels.description: Weekly adoption against deployment frequency, on the weeks where both exist.

panels.title: Adoption vs change failure rate

targets.rawSql:
WITH a AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1000000000), '%x-W%v') AS wk,
       SUM(status='assisted')*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS adoption
FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY wk),
     m AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(cdc.finished_date, '%x-W%v') AS wk,
       SUM(cdc.result='FAILURE')*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS metric
FROM cicd_deployment_commits cdc
JOIN project_mapping pm ON cdc.cicd_scope_id = pm.row_id AND pm.`table` = 'cicd_scopes'
WHERE cdc.environment='PRODUCTION' GROUP BY wk)
SELECT a.wk AS `week`, ROUND(a.adoption,1) AS `adoption %`, ROUND(m.metric,1) AS `failure rate %`
FROM a JOIN m ON a.wk = m.wk ORDER BY a.wk

panels.description: Weekly adoption against change failure rate, on the weeks where both exist.

panels.title: Adoption vs pr cycle time

targets.rawSql:
WITH a AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1000000000), '%x-W%v') AS wk,
       SUM(status='assisted')*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS adoption
FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY wk),
     m AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(pr_merged_date, '%x-W%v') AS wk,
       AVG(pr_cycle_time)/60.0 AS metric
FROM project_pr_metrics WHERE pr_cycle_time IS NOT NULL GROUP BY wk)
SELECT a.wk AS `week`, ROUND(a.adoption,1) AS `adoption %`, ROUND(m.metric,1) AS `cycle time hrs`
FROM a JOIN m ON a.wk = m.wk ORDER BY a.wk

panels.description: Weekly adoption against pr cycle time, on the weeks where both exist.

panels.title: r — adoption vs deployment frequency

targets.rawSql:
WITH a AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1000000000), '%x-W%v') AS wk,
       SUM(status='assisted')*100.0/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS adoption
FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY wk),
     m AS (SELECT DATE_FORMAT(cdc.finished_date, '%x-W%v') AS wk,
       COUNT(DISTINCT cdc.cicd_deployment_id) AS metric
FROM cicd_deployment_commits cdc
JOIN project_mapping pm ON cdc.cicd_scope_id = pm.row_id AND pm.`table` = 'cicd_scopes'
WHERE cdc.result='SUCCESS' AND cdc.environment='PRODUCTION' GROUP BY wk),
     p AS (SELECT a.adoption x, m.metric y FROM a JOIN m ON a.wk = m.wk)
SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) < 10 THEN NULL
            ELSE ROUND((COUNT(*)*SUM(x*y) - SUM(x)*SUM(y)) /
                 NULLIF(SQRT((COUNT(*)*SUM(x*x) - POW(SUM(x),2)) *
                             (COUNT(*)*SUM(y*y) - POW(SUM(y),2))), 0), 2)
       END AS v
FROM p

panels.description: Withheld until 10 overlapping weeks exist.

FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY wk),

JOIN project_mapping pm ON cdc.cicd_scope_id = pm.row_id AND pm.`table` = 'cicd_scopes'
